subject: MAP cost sanity check & eval timeline — CardioSense POC
messages:
From: Gina Smith <gina.smith@cardiosense.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP + token econ sanity check for POC

Hi Hannah / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at CardioSense is excited to move toward a short POC. Before we lock calendar time for the eval, procurement is asking for a mutual action plan (MAP) that includes an explicit cost model and acceptance criteria. Two specific asks from our finance/ops folks:

- A conservative tokens-per-interaction estimate for a standard clinical workflow (this includes system prompt + one user turn + model tokens).
- Recommendations and assumptions for caching and batching (we have a mix of synchronous UI calls and asynchronous bulk-processing).

Rough numbers from our side: ~350k end-user interactions/month, average conversation ~800 tokens, peak concurrency small but bursts up to ~200 req/s. We plan to store templates and some patient-specific metadata server-side and would prefer prefix caching if that helps.

Can you put together a short MAP draft with a simple tokens/$ table, gating milestones for the POC, and an evaluation timeline (2–3 weeks preferred)? We need this for our procurement review to approve the POC spend.

Attaching the product flow and a small sample of user prompts.

Thanks,
Gina Smith
Director, Product Operations
CardioSense

Attachments: cardiosense_flow_v1.pdf (diagram), sample_prompts.txt
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Gina Smith <gina.smith@cardiosense.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MAP + token econ sanity check for POC

Hi Gina — thanks for the clear ask and the sample prompts. I sketched a compact MAP and an evaluation checklist that should get procurement comfortable and give you measurable pass/fail gates for the POC. Key points below; I attached a one-page MAP draft and a token-econ workbook for the telemetry exercises.

High-level assumptions (please confirm):
- Baseline model: open-quant Llama-3-70B-quant (we'll provide a hosted variant). Pricing assumption used for MAP: $0.0006 per 1k input tokens + $0.0012 per 1k output tokens (example blended).
- Tokens/request: system prompt 120 tokens (cached/pinned), average user turn 280 tokens, model output 400 tokens => ~800 tokens total.
- Caching: prefix caching on the system prompt + any static template expected to reduce input tokens by ~15–22% depending on template reuse. We model three scenarios: low (10%), mid (20%), high (35%) cache hit.
- Batching: for async bulk jobs we expect batching up to size 4 with improved GPU utilization; assume batching reduces per-token server cost by ~18–25% in the mid-case. For sync UI paths we assume batching is not applicable (latency SLO).

POC evaluation plan (2 weeks recommended):
1) Week 1 — smoke runs: 5000 sample requests (varied lengths) to measure tokens per response, cache hit rates, and latencies.
2) Week 2 — scaled run: soak test at representative QPS to validate throughput & cost per 100k tokens; run at least one day of burst profile.

Acceptance criteria (examples):
- Mean tokens/request within +/-15% of MAP mid-case.
- Average 95p latency for UI flows < 400ms (hosted) or agreed SLO for private deployments.
- Unit cost per 1k tokens <= the MAP mid-case adjusted price (tbd in final doc).

Immediate asks from CardioSense so we can finalize numbers:
- 3 representative sample prompts for each flow (UI quick query, clinical note generation, async batch classification).
- Expected daily/weekly traffic profile (not just monthly aggregate).

I attached: cardiosense_map_draft_v1.pdf (MAP outline) and token-econ-workbook.xlsx (workbook with scenario tabs). Happy to jump on a quick 30m tomorrow to walk through.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Solutions Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: cardiosense_map_draft_v1.pdf, token-econ-workbook.xlsx

Gina, Hannah — quick follow-ups and internal clarifications: 
- Model variant: recommend we propose a quantized Llama-3 variant for the MAP mid-case and include an optional higher-accuracy variant for quality regression tests. That gives a clear cost/quality tradeoff to CardioSense.
- Cache hit-rate scenarios: include 25%/40%/60% for conservative/mid/aggressive in the workbook. We'll run the smoke tests to measure realistic hits — do you have template reuse metrics?
- Measurement plan: we should instrument token counters at the gateway and correlate with server-side token logs (we'll supply a small telemetry agent).
- Pre-close gating: procurement sign-off, security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence), two-day cost smoke test, and an agreed rollback plan.

Timeline note (internal): to hit CardioSense procurement calendar we're shooting for a 2026-09-24 close. That means: MAP finalized by 2026-09-15, POC start 2026-09-16, and final evaluation complete by 2026-09-30. Can we confirm those milestones?

Ben Carter
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

- We'll provide the three sample prompt sets and a weekly traffic profile export by EOD tomorrow.

- Procurement is OK with the proposed timeline if we have the MAP doc by 2026-09-15. Please include a short table in the MAP that shows cost for low/mid/high cache hit and batching enabled/disabled (a 3x3 matrix).

Next steps: once we have the final MAP and workbook we can route to procurement and security. Also include a link to any shared test credentials or test workspace we should use for the smoke runs (SSO or temporary API key will work).

Gina Smith
